title: 10 Keyboard Shortcuts Every Translator Should Know

10 vital keyboard shortcuts for translators

March 31, 2021
Good to Know | Professional Translation | Translation skills

Translators often work to tight deadlines, and when every minute counts, small habits make a real difference. A handful of keyboard shortcuts can save you seconds on every task, and those seconds add up over a long project.

These shortcuts are for Windows. On a Mac, most of them work with the Cmd key in place of Ctrl, while a few, such as the clipboard history, are Windows only.

Is there a keyboard shortcut to translate text?

This is the question behind many searches for a translate shortcut or a translator hotkey. In Microsoft Word, translation sits on the Review tab, under Translate. In Chrome, you use the translate icon in the address bar when a page is in another language.

Some browser extensions let you assign your own key for translating a page or a selection. If you use one, check where your text goes first, because many tools send it to a third party. Never paste confidential client text into a free tool.

Professional translators work in specialist translation software with its own shortcut list, which you can find in the tool's settings. For everything else, the shortcuts below cover most of your day.

The big hitters

Ctrl + Z and Ctrl + Y

These two shortcuts go hand in hand. Ctrl + Z undoes your last action, so if you accidentally delete a sentence you have spent minutes perfecting, press these two keys and it reappears.

Ctrl + Y redoes the action you just undid. Perhaps you thought it over and the sentence you recovered no longer meets your standards. Press Ctrl and Y, and it is gone again. Both work in most programmes, not only in Word.

Ctrl + A

This shortcut selects everything in the window or document you are in. It saves you scrolling through a 60-page file to copy all of the content, and it works in Word, PDF and Excel files, on web pages and in many other programmes.

Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V

These are better known as copy and paste, and they are indispensable for any computer user, translators included. Highlight the text, press Ctrl + C, place your cursor where you want the text and press Ctrl + V.

Ctrl + V also pastes images and emojis, so you can move more than text between files.

The unsung heroes

Windows key + V

Have you ever lost a word or an image you copied an hour ago? Windows key + V opens the clipboard history, which shows the items you copied with Ctrl + C. You may need to turn the feature on the first time you use it.

Move through the list with the arrow keys, choose the item you want and press Enter to paste it.

Ctrl + Shift + N

Is your file explorer a sea of documents? Ctrl + Shift + N creates a new folder in File Explorer and lets you name it straight away. That makes it easy to set up a folder and subfolders for each client, language and project.

A tidy, dedicated workspace helps you work more efficiently, and that includes your digital one. If you are unsure where the Shift key is, see the section below.

F2

You have created and named your folder, and a typo has slipped into the name. Click on the folder or file and press F2 to rename it, type the correction and press Enter.

It works for any file or folder in File Explorer, so you can keep your naming system consistent without reaching for the mouse.

Alt + Shift or Windows key + Space

If you add a second language to your keyboard to type accents or another alphabet, you need a quick way to switch between layouts. On many Windows setups, Alt + Shift switches the input language, and Ctrl + Shift switches the keyboard layout. Windows key + Space does the same job and works on a standard installation.

You can check or change the shortcut in the advanced keyboard settings under Time and language in Windows Settings. This matters when you work with different languages, as each has its own keyboard layout, whatever the letters printed on your keys.

Windows key + Shift + S

This shortcut lets you select an area of the screen and copy it as a screenshot to the clipboard. It is useful when you need to send a client a query about a layout problem, or capture a term in context for a glossary.

If you only need the window you are working in, press Alt + Print Screen instead. In both cases, paste the image with Ctrl + V into an email or document.

Two extras for consistent terminology

Ctrl + F opens a search box in Word, in your browser and in most other programmes, so you can find every use of a term. Ctrl + H opens find and replace in Word, which helps you apply a client's preferred term across a whole document. Check the results before you accept a global change.

Hotkeys and the Shift key explained

A hotkey is another word for a keyboard shortcut: a key or combination of keys that triggers an action. The Shift key is found on both sides of the letter keys, directly above the Ctrl key at each bottom corner. On many keyboards it is marked with an upward-pointing arrow rather than the word.

Work faster, deliver better

These shortcuts will not translate for you, but they free up time for the part of the job that matters: choosing the right words. They help many translators meet deadlines, and meeting deadlines is a point of pride for BeTranslated.

If you need to translate your website content or documents, our team of professional translators will take care of it. For questions, or a free, no-obligation quote, use our quote request page or get in touch today.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a keyboard shortcut to translate text?

Word and Chrome offer translation through menus, in Word on the Review tab and in Chrome through the address bar icon. Some extensions let you set your own key, but check where they send your text before using them for client work.

What is a hotkey for a translator?

A hotkey is another name for a keyboard shortcut. For translators, the most useful ones are copy and paste, undo and redo, find and replace, and the shortcut that switches your keyboard language.

How do you switch keyboard language in Windows?

Press Windows key + Space to move through your installed input languages. Many setups also use Alt + Shift, which you can check in the advanced keyboard settings.

Which key is the Shift key?

The Shift key sits on both sides of the letter keys, above the Ctrl key in the bottom corners. It is usually marked with an upward-pointing arrow.

Do these shortcuts work on a Mac?

Most of them do, using the Cmd key in place of Ctrl, for example Cmd + Z to undo and Cmd + C to copy. Windows only shortcuts, such as Windows key + V, have different equivalents on a Mac.
